audit.note: every button press carries the pressed control's own text - control_global MESSAGE_TOAST.show with a {0} template filled by ${$source>/text} - and the ActionSheet is a real fragment anchored via popover_display. Corrected 2026-08-21: the note still described per-button HARDCODED text and pointed at an IMPROVISED deviation that no longer exists, contradicting the deviation beside it.

deviations.what: Both halves of the controller are now reproduced instead of faked. (a) onPress toasts oEvent.getSource().getText(); the port transports that value - control_global MESSAGE_TOAST.show with the template '{0}' filled by ${$source>/text} (the app-003 shape) - instead of hardcoding each button's caption, so the icon-only Print button toasts its (empty) text exactly as the original does. (b) onOpen Fragment.loads ActionSheet.fragment.xml and calls openBy(button): the port rebuilds that fragment 1:1 in on_event (ActionSheet title 'Menu', showCancelButton, placement Top, the five Buttons with their icons and visible bindings) and anchors it with client->popover_display( by_id = $event.oSource.sId ) - the overflow Button therefore fires a real backend event instead of a placeholder 'Overflow' toast. The fragment's {range>/isPhone} / {range>/isPhoneOrTablet} bindings fold onto the default model like the view's (a new isphone field joins the existing range flags).

The original drives the toolbar and ActionSheet visibility from a separate 'range' media JSON model (isNoPhone, isNotPhoneOrTablet, isTablet, isPhoneOrTablet, isPhone), seeded from Device.media.getCurrentRange('Std') and kept current by an attachHandler on that range set. **Reworked 2026-08-23**: the flags are UI5 expression bindings over the framework's own device> model - {= ${device>/media/range} === 'Phone' } and friends - which reads the SAME 'Std' range set and is refreshed on every resize (CAPABILITIES; models.js). Until then the port seeded the five flags once with the desktop values and nothing ever wrote them again, which did not just freeze the layout: isPhoneOrTablet was false forever, so the overflow Button that opens the ActionSheet was permanently invisible, its OPEN_SHEET event could never fire, and the 40-line ActionSheet rebuild in on_event was dead code - in a sample whose whole subject is 'toolbar items displayed depending on the current device'. The justification given for the seeding ('a client-only decision') named a limitation the framework does not have.
